chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled in the case of a man who sold a palm tree but stipulated for himself one palm tree from it, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled for him the entrance to it, the exit, and the length of its fronds.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a buyer when the seller retains a portion of the sold property?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Prophet’s practical application of *haqq al-sharik* (rights of co-ownership) in property transactions, ensuring that retaining a portion does not render the buyer’s share unusable. It establishes the legal principle of *madakhil* (access ways) and *makharij* (exit ways) as essential components of ownership, a concept later expanded by Shia jurists to include the span of fronds (*mada jara'id*) to prevent obstruction. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on preventing *gharar* (uncertainty) and ensuring equitable utility in commercial contracts.
